title: NEOWISE hot-dust detections show no clear kinematic contrast after brightness adjustment in 49 centred dwarfs
abstract: We test the kinematic contrast in a published sample of 49 centred dwarfs with a W2 dust excess of at least 20 percent. Young-like stars have 10 detections in 16 stars; field stars have 6 in 33. The young-like group is 1.15 mag brighter at W2. The raw young-like/field odds ratio is 7.50. A brightness adjustment gives 1.97 (95 percent profile interval 0.33-10.66). A model that also uses excess and ecliptic latitude gives 2.29 (0.37-13.49). An exact test within brightness and excess bins gives 1.18 (exact 95 percent interval 0.086-9.72). It expects 9.83 young-like detections under equal odds and observes 10. Alternative bins and selection checks retain large uncertainty. The full 180-star sample still has an adjusted association, so the null result is limited to the hot-excess sample. The data do not establish equal rates or an age-independent dust source. We supply code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and independent numerical checks. No new sky data are added.
